title: Joint Identification of Variable Partitions and Graphs in Grouped Additive-Noise Models
banked_reason: The partial-function identified set excludes only empty-DAG ambiguity, one three-coordinate crossed single-edge pattern, and parent-closed root refinements; arbitrary crossings and externally parented refinements remain open, so the sound ambiguity frontier is subfield rather than field.
gap_reasons: Population identification of the generating causal-unit partition is not proved: the domain of the recovery map may contain multiple incomparable or refinement-related partitions.

The new cross-partition results exclude only unequal empty-DAG factorizations, one three-coordinate crossed single-edge pattern, and coarse-root refinements whose fine blocks have no external parents; arbitrary crossings and externally parented refinements remain open.
The delivered result is a narrow ambiguity frontier rather than the requested identification theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the empty-DAG partition theorem, a smooth-positive three-coordinate crossed-single-edge exclusion, and a root/fine-parent-closed strict-refinement exclusion, while preserving fixed-partition DAG uniqueness from the cited GANM result. It could not globalize the crossing argument through conditioning on correlated competing innovations or cancel external fine-parent terms under the stated class. The surviving identified-set/ambiguity-frontier result is sound and citation-verified, but those unresolved cases keep it below the field novelty floor.
tldr: Acyclic grouped additive-noise mechanisms with mutually independent smooth positive block innovations induce a strictly positive \(C^3\) observed density. Innovation atomicity rules out internal directional additive-noise splits, but under the current assumptions it does not by itself construct such a split from every competing partition. The unconditional population result is therefore an identified set: for each admissible coordinate partition, the law determines one labelled block DAG. Three ambiguity configurations are excluded rigorously: unequal empty-DAG partitions, the relabelled three-coordinate crossed single-edge pair, and a strict refinement in which the coarse block is a root and its fine constituent blocks have no external parents. Arbitrary incomparable crossings and strict refinements with external fine parents remain open. The characteristic-function and covariance diagnostics remain sufficient falsification tools, and the open five-parameter vector family establishes a genuinely non-scalar frontier; no finite certificate, genericity, or unknown-partition uniqueness claim is made.
gap: Göbler, Windisch, and Drton identify a GANM DAG only after the vector partition is supplied, while Peters et al. identify a restricted ANM DAG only on supplied scalar vertices. Entner and Hoyer assume known groups in a linear model with mutually independent group disturbances, use non-Gaussianity for their LiNGAM-based guarantees, and recover a causal order rather than a coordinate partition. Wahl, Ninad, and Runge leave joint partition-and-graph learning open, and the joint-learning algorithms of Niu, Li, and Li and Rajpal et al. do not exclude a second unequal population partition, whether crossed or strictly finer.
fill: The project derives observed-density positivity and \(C^3\) regularity from the triangular structural map. It fixes the residual-law quantifier as \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}(m)\), proves that full positivity implies affine nondegeneracy, and supplies a splitwise characteristic-function modulus criterion for atomicity; finite-moment covariance variation is retained only as a sufficient directional diagnostic whose failure to detect variation proves nothing. The three-coordinate crossing uses conull regular slices and differentiates only a continuous log-ratio identity. The nondescendant overlap-cell and extremal finer-block quotient handles address incomparable and strictly comparable partitions separately. The labelled DAG then follows from the cited fixed-partition theorem using the published Equation (3). The comparator frontier uses the open family \((a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda)\in(0,\infty)^5\), with normalization, dependence, and both directional exclusions proved by conditional-variance monotonicity.
